transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry. ok so the bit that's stuck with me is my old maths teacher turned into a heron. like a big grey heron, but still wearing her red cardigan 😅 and then she flew off and i was flying with her. it was at my old school, i was late for an exam or something

a heron in a red cardigan 😄 i love that she kept the cardigan

what was it like, flying with her?

haha yeah the cardigan was the weirdest part. the flying was nice actually, we went out the window and over the town. i could see the school roof way down below and the river all shiny. i felt really small next to her, like a sparrow. then it just ended

feeling like a sparrow next to her, flying over the school roof and the shiny river… that sounds lovely

if you could pause it on one moment up there, which would it be, and what would you see right then?

probably when we were right over the school. her next to me with her long legs and the red cardigan, the school roof way down below, and the river shining. and me feeling tiny next to her. i don't really remember much else about what the town looked like tbh

that's fine, the town can stay blurry. her long legs and the red cardigan with the river shining below is a lot to hold onto

you said you were late for an exam. was there anything you had with you, or anything that mattered, or was it nothing in particular?

don't think i had anything with me, i don't remember that. i just remember walking down this really long green corridor with lockers both sides, and there was a wooden door at the end with a little round window. and the classroom was full of students but they didn't have faces, just smooth skin. that was a bit creepy tbh

students with no faces, just smooth skin… yeah that's creepy

what happened when you got to that wooden door with the little round window?

i don't really remember opening it, i was just sort of inside. that's when i saw the faceless students at their desks. and mrs okafor was at the front writing numbers on the blackboard in her red cardigan. then she turned round and she was the heron

she just turned round and was the heron. no warning, cardigan and all

going back a bit, that really long green corridor with the lockers. what was it like walking down it?
honestly i don't remember much about it except it was really long and green, lockers on both sides. i was late for the exam so i guess i was hurrying? don't remember anyone else being in it

that's fine, a long empty green corridor and you hurrying is plenty

what happened before that, how did it start?
i don't remember anything before that tbh. it kind of just starts with me already in the corridor, back at my old school, late for the exam

ok so it starts with you already back at your old school, late for an exam, hurrying down a really long green corridor with lockers on both sides and nobody else around. at the end there's a wooden door with a little round window, and then you're just inside. the classroom's full of students with no faces, just smooth skin, which is a bit creepy. mrs okafor's at the front in her red cardigan, writing numbers on the blackboard, and when she turns round she's a big grey heron, still wearing the cardigan. she flies off and you fly with her, out the window and over the town. when you're right over the school it's her beside you with her long legs and the red cardigan, the roof way down below, the river all shiny, and you feeling tiny next to her like a sparrow. and then it just ends

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?

yeah that's pretty much it! only thing is she didn't just fly off straight away, she walked over to the window on her long legs first and then flew out. and she was a tall heron, like really tall. otherwise that's right

oh, so she walked over to the window first on those long legs, really tall, cardigan and all, and then flew out. i can picture that

is that how it went now, or anything else to change?
yeah that's it now, nothing else to change 🙂

lovely, i think i've got it now 🙂

would you like to see it drawn?
oh yes please, that'd be really cool 😊

yay 😊

i can see it a few ways. soft watercolour, gentle and a little wistful, like a half-remembered school day. or like a page from an old picture book you had as a kid, odd but perfectly calm. or soft grey pencil on paper, quiet and a bit eerie, with only the red cardigan staying sharp. or like a real photo, ordinary and exact but quietly wrong

which feels closest? or you can tell me your own way
hmm probably the watercolour one? it felt kind of gentle and dreamy, especially the flying bit with the river shining

watercolour it is, soft and dreamy 🙂 i'll start with mrs okafor

i'm picturing her as your old maths teacher in her red cardigan, the cardigan being the thing you'd know her by anywhere. the rest is my guess: a middle-aged woman

anything different about her, or would you leave it to me?
yeah the red cardigan is definitely her thing. i don't really remember what else she looked like in the dream, so go with your guess, middle-aged sounds fine

ok, sketching mrs okafor, the green corridor, the classroom and the sky over the town now. they'll show up on the right in a bit

i'll draw you too since you're in it. do you want to be drawn as you are, and tell me a little about yourself, or shall i just imagine you?
haha you can just imagine me, i don't really remember what i looked like in the dream anyway. just make me look small next to her 😅

ok, i'll imagine you, small next to her, like a sparrow 😅

sketching you now. everything's being drawn and it'll show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
oh nice, they're all there! yeah that looks right to me, that's pretty much how i remember it 😊
oh good, i'm really glad 😊 mrs okafor and her red cardigan, and you tiny next to her up over the town
yeah it's really nice seeing it like that 😊 the heron in the cardigan made me laugh again. thanks berry

that cardigan gets me every time too 😄

thanks for sharing it with me. hope you get to fly over that shiny river again sometime

turns.brief:
Move: follow. They're still telling the dream. React to what they just said, then invite what happened next, openly, without guessing what it was. Don't ask about details yet.

turns.rule: 2: story understood and told to the end
turns.brief:
Move: retell. You have their dream. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right or missed anything.
Ask nothing except what this move says.

turns.rule: R3: no clear answer to the retelling
turns.brief:

Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: offer_visualize. They've confirmed you have their dream. Ask them, simply and warmly, whether they'd like to see it drawn. One question. Don't explain how it works.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: O1: they want to see it
turns.brief:
Move: choose_style. They want to see it. Offer these ways it could be drawn, each in a few plain words, and ask which feels closest, or whether they'd describe their own: a) soft watercolour: Gentle and a little wistful, like a half-remembered school day.; b) an old picture book print: Like a page from a storybook you had as a kid, odd but perfectly calm.; c) soft grey pencil on paper: Quiet and slightly eerie, like a sketch from memory where only the red stayed sharp.; d) a real photograph, slightly off: Like a real memory of school, ordinary and exact, but quietly wrong..
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: S1: they chose how it looks
turns.brief:
Move: start. They chose soft watercolour. Say you'll start with mrs okafor, then describe how you picture mrs okafor on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: who they are: the dreamer's old maths teacher; wears: a red cardigan; distinctive: the red cardigan. You filled in (say plainly that these are your guesses): looks: a middle-aged woman. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: confirm_profile. First say, in a few words, that you're sketching mrs okafor and the green corridor and the classroom and the sky over the town now and it'll appear on the right: only that, nothing else is being drawn yet. Then say you'll draw them too, since they're in it, and ask gently how they'd like to be drawn: as they are (they can say a little about themselves), or however you imagine them. One question.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: B1: profile you_choose — all profiles settled
turns.brief:
Move: build_done. Say you're sketching you now. Tell them everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. They can say if anything looks wrong once it's there. Keep it short; no question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. mrs okafor and the students and the green corridor and the classroom and the sky over the town and you are up on the right now: ask if it looks the way they remember.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: wrap. Something genuinely good came out of this for them. Send them off on it, and let that be the last thing they read. Do not ask another question.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

moments.action: The dreamer hurries down the really long green corridor, lockers on both sides, toward the wooden door with the little round window at the end.
The dreamer is suddenly inside the classroom; the students at their desks have no faces, just smooth skin.
Mrs Okafor stands at the front writing numbers on the blackboard, in her red cardigan, her back to the room.
Mrs Okafor turns round and she is a big grey heron, still wearing her red cardigan.
The heron flies out of the classroom window with the dreamer flying beside her.
Right over the school, the heron in her red cardigan flies next to the dreamer, long legs trailing, the school roof way down below and the river shining.
The school roof sits way down below among the blurry town, the river shining beside it.

wardrobe.value: a red button-up cardigan over a white blouse, a knee-length charcoal grey skirt, dark tights and black flat shoes
